Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that handles partial and final streaming recognition events using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Option 2 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 3 — Cloud Speech streaming:
  Service: Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming
  SDK: google-cloud-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: streaming_recognize
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/speech-to-text-requests#streaming

Option 4 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 5 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Option 6 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import websockets

async def deepgram_speech_to_text_streaming(audio_stream):
    """
    Handles streaming speech-to-text using Deepgram.

    Args:
        audio_stream: An asynchronous generator or stream yielding audio chunks (bytes).
    """
    DEEPGRAM_API_KEY = os.environ.get("DEEPGRAM_API_KEY")
    if not DEEPGRAM_API_KEY:
        raise ValueError("DEEPGRAM_API_KEY environment variable not set.")

    # Deepgram API endpoint for streaming recognition
    # Model used: enhanced, language: en-US, punctuate: true, interim_results: true
    # For more options, see https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets
    deepgram_url = (
        "wss://api.deepgram.com/v1/listen?encoding=linear16&sample_rate=16000&"
        "model=nova-2&language=en-US&punctuate=true&interim_results=true"
    )

    async with websockets.connect(
        deepgram_url,
        extra_headers={'Authorization': f'Token {DEEPGRAM_API_KEY}'}
    ) as websocket:
        # Send audio data from the stream
        async def send_audio():
            async for chunk in audio_stream:
                if chunk:
                    await websocket.send(chunk)
            # Signal the end of the audio stream
            await websocket.send(json.dumps({"type": "CloseStream"}))

        # Receive transcripts from Deepgram
        async def receive_transcripts():
            try:
                async for message in websocket:
                    response = json.loads(message)
                    if response.get('type') == 'Results':
                        transcript = response['channel']['alternatives'][0]['transcript']
                        is_final = response['is_final']

                        if transcript:
                            if is_final:
                                print(f"Final Transcript: {transcript}")
                            else:
                                print(f"Partial Transcript: {transcript}")
            except websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK:
                print("Deepgram WebSocket connection closed normally.")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error receiving transcripts: {e}")

        # Run sending and receiving concurrently
        await asyncio.gather(send_audio(), receive_transcripts())

# Example of how to use it with a dummy audio stream
async def generate_dummy_audio_chunks():
    """Generates dummy audio chunks for demonstration."""
    # In a real application, this would read from a microphone, file, etc.
    print("Simulating audio stream... (sending 10 chunks)")
    for i in range(1, 11):
        # Simulate 1 second of silence (linear16, 16kHz, 16-bit mono)
        # 16000 samples/sec * 2 bytes/sample = 32000 bytes/sec
        chunk_size = 32000 // 10 # 1/10th of a second
        yield b'\x00' * chunk_size # Send silence
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1) # Simulate real-time delay
    print("Finished simulating audio stream.")
